content:
Last month we ran a poll, and the vast majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should exit the advertising business.

Advertising has now arrived in Apple Maps in the US and Canada, and I think it's just as distasteful as you imagine...

Apple previewed this back in March, saying ads would appear in the Maps app sometime this summer. We finally got a look at what the ads actually look like yesterday, and Apple confirmed that the ads have started rolling out over the past few days. All users in the US and Canada will see the ads over the next few weeks.

  • Before search: Sponsored suggestions will appear under the 'Featured Places' column on the search page.
  • After search: Ads will appear alongside relevant search results.

Apple says privacy is one of their priorities.

I believe that, but I still find the whole thing tacky, for two reasons.

Featured comment by John Atkinson:

The only reason I can think of that has nothing to do with ad revenue is that adding ads to Apple Maps might encourage more businesses to claim their business pages. Apple Maps has never been able to catch up with Google Maps, and one long-standing reason is that many businesses simply don't want to spend the time adding themselves to the map, or letting their information become outdated. In North America, because iPhone penetration is high, this isn't a major issue, but overseas it absolutely is.

In theory, ads could serve as an incentive for businesses to upload their information, since they can advertise in the same app (or, in order to advertise, their marketing teams will fill in all the information). But I'm not sure I believe that's Apple's reason for doing this? Absolutely not—it's clearly to make more money—but at least there's a side benefit of improving the quality of map data.

First, although Apple won't deliver personalised ads to you through any form of tracking, almost every other app and website does. Most people naturally assume the iPhone maker does too—no matter how unfair that perception is—and that hurts Apple's reputation for protecting user privacy.

Second, it's just plain tacky. In the app and online publishing ecosystem, advertising is a necessary evil: precisely because of ads, free apps or websites can keep running. But Apple certainly doesn't need ad revenue to pay the rent: their premium hardware is already priced very high. Advertising simply doesn't fit Apple's brand image.

I recall John Gruber once likened ads in Apple apps to those hideous Intel Inside stickers on cheap Windows laptops. Of course we understand that companies making cheap laptops need to chase every possible revenue source, but we never expect Apple to slap the same kind of sticker on a MacBook and lower the brand's standing. So how can we accept ads appearing in native apps on Apple devices?

My position remains the same as always: Apple simply shouldn't be in the advertising business.
